title: Tower base-change data, counit mates and reduction predicates
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Use the ordinary derived strict coefficient-tower categories and uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], with section-normalized coefficient-tower coordinates and geometric operations [def-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-interfaces], realized by the section-normalized base, operations and extension-by-zero exchange of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. For a Cartesian square $fu=vf'$ of schemes and a compactification $c$ of $f$, use its pullback compactification [def-cbc-compact-support-square] and the constant-ring derived pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Define Data to record constructibility/Tor membership certificates for the two compact-support functors and horizontal tower and finite pullbacks, the two right-adjoint functors, their adjunctions, and their unit/counit-normalized finite comparison data [def-sp-tower-gluing-interfaces]. Define U and V as the restrictions of the actual horizontal tower pullbacks. Define composition by cancelling the middle realization equivalence, exchange by transporting the actual compactification exchange through these equivalences, and beta as its restriction to the full constructible finite-Tor categories. Assuming beta invertible, define mate as mateEquiv of its inverse, equivalently the primed unit followed by the primed right adjoint applied to inverse beta and the pulled-back counit. Define finiteP and finiteQ by the mixed finite constructible pullback of [det-sp-mixed-base-change] and the recorded finite right adjoints, finiteExchange by the actual finite compactification exchange of that node on the chosen Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with finite compact support [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison], and finiteMate by the corresponding finite adjunction transpose when that exchange component is invertible. Define pullEvaluation, sourceComparison and targetComparison by the published evaluation and gluing comparisons. For a quotient from positive level n to positive level m with m<=n, use the derived scalar functors [sk-def-sp-scalar-extension] and [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], the finite constructible scalar reduction [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] and canonical scalar/pullback identification [def-sp-constant-scalar-pullback-comparison]. Define coefficient as the gluing counit coefficient mate, sourceCoefficient and targetCoefficient by these scalar/pullback identifications and coefficient mates, inputReduction as the actual tower transition, and sourceReduction and targetReduction as the actual reductions transported through the finite evaluation comparisons. Finally define Laws as the proposition recording the explicit compact-support evaluation equation, counit-transpose formula, finite mate evaluation, source and target reduction equations, mixed coefficient equation and full three-equality reduction chain including the input transition. This defines a predicate; it asserts neither that Laws holds nor that any mate or comparison is invertible. All natural-number levels n denote the positive exponent n+1, and unnormalized towers are allowed.
